findings.description: The database password is interpolated directly into EC2 user data and written to a PHP configuration file on the instance. User data can be retrieved by principals with access to the instance or its metadata/user-data interfaces, and the credential remains on disk in application configuration.

The application connects with mysqli_connect using only the RDS endpoint, username, and password; no TLS/SSL options or certificate validation are configured. Database credentials and application data may therefore traverse the network without transport encryption if the database accepts non-TLS connections.

The RDS instance is configured with publicly_accessible = true, assigning it a public network endpoint. Although the shown security-group ingress is limited to the VPC CIDR, this unnecessarily exposes the database to public routing and increases attack surface if network controls change or additional rules are introduced.
storage_encrypted = false leaves database storage and associated snapshots unencrypted at rest, exposing catalog data if underlying storage or snapshots are accessed.
The database administrator username is fixed as "admin" in configuration. This provides a predictable privileged account name and weakens resistance to credential-guessing attacks.

The policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on every resource. Attached to the application role, this violates least privilege and permits broad data access, infrastructure modification, and potential privilege-escalation actions if the application instance or role credentials are compromised.
